takeaway: Tropical Wave #47 is over Costa Rica today — expect a partly cloudy morning, then stronger afternoon showers and storms across the northern Pacific, with some coastal rain possible into the evening. Surf winds: early-morning easterly help, then Pacific onshore later today and Sunday (choppier faces). Midweek looks cleaner as Caribbean trades rebuild. Distant East Pacific storms stay well off Mexico; prolonged multi-day rain is still a watch, not locked in.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sat–Mon)
periods.pattern: Saturday is the wetter day of the weekend as Wave #47 crosses with the usual rainy-season heat: morning partly cloudy, afternoon storms over Pacífico Norte, and scattered night rain possible on the coast. Hot inland (Nicoya around 32°C, Liberia near 36°C). Sunday stays showery but a notch quieter than Saturday. Winds: light easterly early, then Pacific south/southwest daytime Sat–Sun; shifting toward north/northwest by Sunday night into Monday.
periods.implications: Plan outdoor time for Saturday morning before storms. For surf, chase night and early-morning lulls — expect choppier faces after mid-morning Sat–Sun. Monday starts the turn toward cleaner offshore quality if the northerly/easterly shift holds.
periods.confidence: High that Saturday is locally stormy and no nearby cyclone hits Costa Rica. Moderate on exact Nosara storm timing and how clean Monday morning gets.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Tue–Fri)
periods.pattern: Official weekly outlook calls for a slight easing of Pacific rains early next week, with more isolated afternoon storms. Ensemble averages keep Nicoya rain mostly light-to-moderate. Low-level flow favors Caribbean easterlies/northeast trades across Nicaragua and Nicoya — a clearer offshore pattern than this weekend. Seas near Papagayo stay about 4–6 ft with north/northwest winds much of the midweek.
periods.implications: Better surf-wind window than the weekend: night/morning glass more reliable, and Nicaragua all-day offshore would support good Nosara quality (still not a guarantee of Nosara all-day offshore). Keep late-day plans flexible for quick storms.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the trade return and quieter theme; low–moderate for any midweek wetter spike if Pacific moisture reconnects.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook still leans drier than normal for the northern Pacific from late September into mid-October, with no official extreme-rain event flagged. Ensemble means show some moist days possible into early October, but without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west.
periods.implications: No prolonged flood-season spell is the baseline for Nicoya Pacific. Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Mainly Saturday–Monday (26–28 Sep) while Wave #47 and Pacific moisture overlap; reassess midweek if a Mexico-side system feeds extra moisture south
gyreWatch.supporting: Wave #47 is over the country today and favors stronger afternoon storms. Friday evening’s official storm notice already flagged wet Saturday totals. Broad moist Pacific flow and a high-odds disturbance south of Tehuantepec could keep the Pacific side juiced. One model family briefly shows a Pacific low closer to Central America around early next week.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages — the pattern is a weekend wave plus distant Mexico systems, not a Costa Rica–centered temporales. Average model rain for Nicoya stays mostly light-to-moderate. Midweek easterly trades argue against a stuck onshore rain machine. The longer official outlook still leans drier for northern Pacific into October.

surfWinds.regime: Mixed: Pacific onshore Sat–Sun days → Caribbean easterlies rebuilding midweek
surfWinds.detail: This morning favors light easterly (offshore) help. Papagayo and ensemble winds turn Pacific south/southwest later today and Sunday — onshore/side-on for west-facing Nosara, so choppier faces. By early next week, Caribbean easterlies look stronger across Nicaragua and Nicoya, which is the classic offshore setup. Nicaragua all-day offshore midweek is a good Nosara quality signal, but it does not mean Nosara stays glassy all day. Do not read Papagayo light/variable as all-day glass.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Overnight and early morning Sat–Sun. Cleaner overnight/morning glass Tue–Fri if trades hold. No clean all-day offshore weekend signal.
surfWinds.confidence: High on weekend daytime onshore; moderate on how firmly trades lock in midweek.

whatChanged: Wave #47 is now over the country (yesterday it was still a weekend threat). New Friday 5:45 p.m. storm notice covers today’s wetter afternoon. Papagayo now shows a clearer S–SW weekend then N/NW midweek turn — so surf winds improve after Sunday night, not during the weekend. Tehuantepec disturbance still ~90% to form but tracks along southern Mexico, not toward Costa Rica. Polo remains well west of Mexico with Odalys and Nolo farther out; nothing near Costa Rica. Longer-range still leans drier for Nicoya Pacific.
practical: Best outdoors: Saturday morning before afternoon storms; keep evening flexible for coastal rain. Heat inland continues. For surf, prioritize night and early-morning sessions this weekend; look for cleaner easterly glass from about Monday–Tuesday onward. Watch Sat–Mon if the wave verifies wetter than average. Latest official storm notice: Friday 5:45 p.m. covering Friday night and Saturday Wave #47.
